content.question: How does the agent select actions in Q-Learning, and how are Q-coefficients updated?
options: Actions are selected using an exploration–exploitation strategy, and after each action the Q-coefficients of the current state-action pair are updated using the Bellman equation.
Actions are selected randomly forever, and Q-coefficients are simply set to one.
Actions are selected only by the highest reward seen so far, and Q-coefficients come from a covariance matrix.
Actions are selected via a hash-tree, and Q-coefficients are pruned below a minimum support threshold.
content.answer: Actions are selected using an exploration–exploitation strategy, and after each action the Q-coefficients of the current state-action pair are updated using the Bellman equation.
